title: The grown-ups who play with toys
paragraphs: We all know children love to play with toys. But as they approach adulthood, they stop being playful and concentrate on grown-up things – or so we believe. However, in recent times at least, adults are revisiting their childhood and buying toys for themselves – and they've been given the nickname 'kidults'.

There are many reasons for the rise of the kidult, but it's certainly big business. In the USA for example, the Toy Association says that over half of adults bought toys and games for themselves last year. Nostalgia is part of the reason: people want to relive their childhood and now have the disposable income to do so. Puzzles and board games are traditional toys that can be enjoyed at any age.

But there's more to being a big kid than just taking a trip down memory lane. People have more time to let their hair down and play. Hobbies such as modelling and construction with plastic bricks can help people develop skills into adulthood. And they allow people to switch off and relax. In fact, Frederique Tutt, global industry analyst at NPD, told the BBC: "I'd say much of this is providing an escape from the stresses and strains of modern-day living, fulfilling our need to find downtime."

Some people are even finding comfort and camaraderie by playing with others. Although competing with others through video gaming might be nothing new, others are coming together to build train sets or sophisticated models. In Brighton in the UK, for example, Brighton Bricks is a club where adult fans of the toy Lego meet up every month to talk, play and swap collections.

But those who think playing with toys is childish and immature should take note of the research by René Proyer, professor of psychology at Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg in Germany. It suggests that adults who demonstrate more playful personality traits are more motivated, creative and spontaneous. So, it seems life shouldn't be all work and no play, and maybe we should take play more seriously!

vocabulary.translation: 你接近小镇时，会看到左边的教堂。

vocabulary.entry: **adulthood** /ˈædʌlthʊd/ n. 成年，成年期（书面语）
vocabulary.example: He lived independently throughout his entire adulthood.
vocabulary.translation: 他整个成年时期都独立生活。

vocabulary.example: We decided to revisit the museum to see the new exhibition.
vocabulary.translation: 我们决定重访博物馆去看新展览。

vocabulary.example: His tall, thin build earned him the nickname 'Spider'.
vocabulary.translation: 他瘦高的身材为他赢得了"蜘蛛"的绰号。

vocabulary.entry: **kidult** /ˈkɪdʌlt/ n. 童心未泯的成年人
vocabulary.example: Toy companies are increasingly marketing their products to kidults.
vocabulary.translation: 玩具公司越来越多地向童心未泯的成年人推销产品。

vocabulary.example: This is certainly the best movie I've seen this year.
vocabulary.translation: 这无疑是我今年看过的最好电影。

vocabulary.example: A wave of nostalgia came over her when she saw the old photographs.
vocabulary.translation: 看到旧照片时，她心中涌起一阵怀旧之情。

vocabulary.entry: **relive** /ˌriːˈlɪv/ v. 重温，再次体验（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Watching the video allows us to relive our wedding day.
vocabulary.translation: 观看视频让我们得以重温婚礼那天。

vocabulary.entry: **disposable income** /dɪˈspəʊzəbl ˈɪnkʌm/ n. 可支配收入
vocabulary.example: Young people today have more disposable income than their parents did.
vocabulary.translation: 如今的年轻人比他们的父母有更多的可支配收入。

vocabulary.example: The child loves to do jigsaw puzzles.
vocabulary.translation: 这个孩子喜欢玩拼图。

vocabulary.entry: **board game** /ˈbɔːd ɡeɪm/ n. 棋盘游戏
vocabulary.example: We spent the evening playing board games like Monopoly.
vocabulary.translation: 我们晚上玩了像大富翁这样的棋盘游戏。

vocabulary.entry: **let one's hair down** /ˌlet wʌnz ˈheə daʊn/ phr. 放松，无拘无束（口语）
vocabulary.example: The party gave everyone a chance to let their hair down.
vocabulary.translation: 派对给了每个人放松的机会。

vocabulary.example: His hobbies include photography and modelling.
vocabulary.translation: 他的爱好包括摄影和模型制作。

vocabulary.example: The bridge is a remarkable work of engineering construction.
vocabulary.translation: 这座桥是建筑工程的一个杰作。

vocabulary.entry: **switch off** /ˌswɪtʃ ˈɒf/ phr. v. 不再注意，放松（口语）
vocabulary.example: When I get home from work, I just want to switch off for a while.
vocabulary.translation: 我下班回家后，只想放松一会儿。

vocabulary.example: A political analyst commented on the election results.
vocabulary.translation: 一位政治分析师评论了选举结果。

vocabulary.example: Reading provides an escape from everyday worries.
vocabulary.translation: 阅读提供了一种摆脱日常烦恼的方式。

vocabulary.example: The recent strain of his work has made him ill.
vocabulary.translation: 最近的工作压力让他生病了。

vocabulary.example: He travelled around the world to fulfil his dreams.
vocabulary.translation: 他环游世界来实现自己的梦想。

vocabulary.entry: **downtime** /ˈdaʊntaɪm/ n. 休息时间，停工时间
vocabulary.example: Everyone needs a bit of downtime to relax.
vocabulary.translation: 每个人都需要一点休息时间来放松。

vocabulary.entry: **camaraderie** /ˌkæməˈrɑːdəri/ n. 友情，同志情谊（书面语）
vocabulary.example: There is a great sense of camaraderie among the team members.
vocabulary.translation: 团队成员之间有着强烈的友情。

vocabulary.entry: **sophisticated** /səˈfɪstɪkeɪtɪd/ adj. 复杂的，精密的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The police use sophisticated equipment to detect criminals.
vocabulary.translation: 警方使用精密设备来侦查罪犯。

vocabulary.example: We swapped phone numbers so we could stay in touch.
vocabulary.translation: 我们交换了电话号码以便保持联系。

vocabulary.entry: **childish** /ˈtʃaɪldɪʃ/ adj. 孩子气的，幼稚的（常含贬义）
vocabulary.example: Don't be so childish – stop fighting over a toy.
vocabulary.translation: 别这么幼稚——别为了一个玩具打架了。

vocabulary.example: It was immature of him to react in that way.
vocabulary.translation: 他那样反应真不成熟。

vocabulary.entry: **take note of** /teɪk nəʊt əv/ phr. 注意，留意
vocabulary.example: Passers-by took note of the smoke coming from the window.
vocabulary.translation: 路人注意到了从窗户冒出的烟。

vocabulary.example: The team demonstrated great skill and determination.
vocabulary.translation: 这支队伍展现了高超的技能和决心。

vocabulary.entry: **personality trait** /ˌpɜːsəˈnæləti treɪt/ n. 人格特质，性格特点（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Honesty is one of her most admirable personality traits.
vocabulary.translation: 诚实是她最令人钦佩的人格特质之一。

vocabulary.example: Our staff are hard-working and highly motivated.
vocabulary.translation: 我们的员工工作努力且积极性很高。

vocabulary.entry: **spontaneous** /spɒnˈteɪniəs/ adj. 自发的，自然流露的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The crowd gave a spontaneous cheer when the news was announced.
vocabulary.translation: 消息宣布时，人群自发地欢呼起来。

sentences.english: We all know children love to play with toys.
sentences.chinese: 我们都知道孩子们喜欢玩玩具。

sentences.english: But as they approach adulthood, they stop being playful and concentrate on grown-up things – or so we believe.
sentences.chinese: 但随着他们长大，他们就不再玩耍，专注于成年人的事情——至少我们是这样认为的。

sentences.english: However, in recent times at least, adults are revisiting their childhood and buying toys for themselves – and they've been given the nickname 'kidults'.
sentences.chinese: 然而，至少近年来，成年人正在重温童年，为自己购买玩具——他们被赋予了一个绰号"童心未泯的成年人"。

sentences.english: There are many reasons for the rise of the kidult, but it's certainly big business.
sentences.chinese: "童心未泯的成年人"现象兴起的原因有很多，但这无疑是大生意。

sentences.english: In the USA for example, the Toy Association says that over half of adults bought toys and games for themselves last year.
sentences.chinese: 例如，在美国，玩具协会表示，去年超过一半的成年人给自己买了玩具和游戏。

sentences.english: Nostalgia is part of the reason: people want to relive their childhood and now have the disposable income to do so.
sentences.chinese: 怀旧是一部分原因：人们想重温童年，现在有了可支配收入来实现这一点。

sentences.english: Puzzles and board games are traditional toys that can be enjoyed at any age.
sentences.chinese: 拼图和棋盘游戏是任何年龄段都可以享受的传统玩具。

sentences.english: But there's more to being a big kid than just taking a trip down memory lane.
sentences.chinese: 但做个"大孩子"不仅仅是一次回忆过去之旅。

sentences.english: People have more time to let their hair down and play.
sentences.chinese: 人们有更多时间放松和玩耍。

sentences.english: Hobbies such as modelling and construction with plastic bricks can help people develop skills into adulthood.
sentences.chinese: 诸如用塑料积木建模和建造之类的爱好可以帮助人们在成年后发展技能。

sentences.english: And they allow people to switch off and relax.
sentences.chinese: 它们还能让人们暂时放下烦恼，放松身心。

sentences.english: In fact, Frederique Tutt, global industry analyst at NPD, told the BBC: "I'd say much of this is providing an escape from the stresses and strains of modern-day living, fulfilling our need to find downtime."
sentences.chinese: 事实上，NPD的全球行业分析师弗雷德里克·图特告诉BBC："我想说，这样做很多时候可以逃避现代生活的压力和紧张，满足我们暂时逃离的需求。"

sentences.english: Some people are even finding comfort and camaraderie by playing with others.
sentences.chinese: 有些人甚至通过与他人一起玩耍找到了慰藉和友情。

sentences.english: Although competing with others through video gaming might be nothing new, others are coming together to build train sets or sophisticated models.
sentences.chinese: 虽然通过电子游戏与他人竞争可能并不新鲜，但其他人则聚在一起建造火车模型或复杂的模型。

sentences.english: In Brighton in the UK, for example, Brighton Bricks is a club where adult fans of the toy Lego meet up every month to talk, play and swap collections.
sentences.chinese: 例如，在英国布莱顿，有一个名为"布莱顿积木"的俱乐部，乐高玩具的成年粉丝们每月聚会一次，聊天、玩耍和交换收藏品。

sentences.english: But those who think playing with toys is childish and immature should take note of the research by René Proyer, professor of psychology at Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg in Germany.
sentences.chinese: 但那些认为玩玩具是幼稚和不成熟的人，应该留意德国哈勒-维滕贝格马丁·路德大学心理学教授勒内·普罗耶的研究。

sentences.english: It suggests that adults who demonstrate more playful personality traits are more motivated, creative and spontaneous.
sentences.chinese: 研究表明，展现出更多玩乐人格特质的成年人更有内驱力、更有创造力、也更自发自觉。

sentences.english: So, it seems life shouldn't be all work and no play, and maybe we should take play more seriously!
sentences.chinese: 所以，生活似乎不应该只工作不玩耍，也许我们应该更认真地对待玩耍！
